name: Forms

hero.title: Type in one field. The other eleven never notice.
hero.lede: Every field's value, error, touched and dirty flag is its own signal, so a keystroke updates one input and nothing else. On a 12-field form against six popular form libraries, it was the fastest at all four timed operations.

why.title: The form code you keep rewriting, already written.

items.title: A keystroke touches one field
items.text: Value, error, touched and dirty are four separate signals per field. Typing in `email` updates the email input and its error text; the password field, the submit button and the other ten fields stay put. Formik re-renders its whole form 10 times for 10 keystrokes; this does 0.

items.title: Async checks can't race
items.text: Async validators are versioned and receive an `AbortSignal`. When the user types faster than your server answers, the late answer is dropped instead of overwriting the newer one. `debounceMs: 300` cuts the requests too.

items.title: Your schema, as it is
items.text: Hand `schema` a raw Zod, Valibot or ArkType schema, or `@pyreon/validate`'s `s`. No resolver package. An error on `address.city` lands on the `address.city` field, and a key that matches no field fails the form instead of vanishing.

items.title: Accessible by default
items.text: One `register('email')` spread gives the input an id, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` that follow the error. A failed submit moves focus to the first broken field, like React Hook Form's `shouldFocusError`.

difference.title: Delete the debounce, the race guard and the effect.

before.label: React, an async check by hand
before.caption: A ref to drop stale answers, a timer to debounce, an effect with a dependency array. Per async field.

after.label: with @pyreon/form
after.caption: Declare the check. Debounce, stale-result discarding and the abort signal are built in.

demo.text: The email check answers after 0.4 to 1.1 seconds, and "ada@example.com" is taken. Type fast and watch the counters: the password field never updates while you type an email, and every slow answer that arrives late is thrown away.

items.name: Two ways to declare
items.text: `useForm({ initialValues })`, or reusable `field('email', '', validator)` definitions passed as `useForm({ fields })`, with the value type inferred either way.

items.name: Validate on blur, change or submit
items.text: `validateOn` defaults to `'blur'`, so nobody is told off mid-word.

items.name: Async validators
items.text: with `debounceMs`, an `AbortSignal`, and stale results discarded by version.

items.name: Cross-field rules
items.text: every validator gets `(value, allValues)`, so "must differ from email" is one line.

items.name: Field arrays with stable keys
items.text: `append`, `prepend`, `insert`, `remove`, `update`, `move`, `swap`, `replace`; render with `<For by={(i) => i.key}>` and inputs keep focus when rows move.

items.name: Dot-path leaf fields
items.text: `'address.city'` is a real field; `nestValues()` turns the flat values into the nested payload your API wants.

items.name: Server errors in one call
items.text: `setErrors({ email: 'Already registered' })` shows them at once, touched or not.

items.name: Reset to what the server saved
items.text: `reset(saved)` makes the saved values the new clean baseline; `keepErrors`, `keepTouched`, `keepDirty` keep what you choose.

items.name: Runtime fields
items.text: `registerField` and `unregisterField` for forms built from data.

limits.title: Validation waits for blur
limits.text: That is the default, so people aren't corrected mid-word. For live feedback set `validateOn: 'change'` and add `debounceMs` if a validator calls your server.

limits.title: Key array rows by `item.key`
limits.text: Each `useFieldArray` item carries a stable `key`. Use it in `<For by>`; an index key makes inputs lose focus when rows move.

limits.title: Dot-path values stay flat
limits.text: `values()` and `onSubmit` keep `'address.city'` as one key. Convert at the API boundary with `nestValues()`; a nested schema needs an `as never` cast until deep-path types land.

limits.title: Typed `<Form of>` in strict TSX
limits.text: Today `<Form of={form}>` rejects a typed form under `strict`. Until that is fixed, write `<form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit}>` or wrap with `<FormProvider form={form}>`, both of which type cleanly.

comingFrom.title: Same shape, minus the resolver and the formState destructure.
comingFrom.note: `register()` reads the same. The Zod schema goes in as it is, and `setErrors` replaces `setError`. Each error line is its own reactive text, so a new error repaints one `<span>`.

comingFrom.title: Keep the validate logic, lose the render prop.
comingFrom.note: Formik's `validate` becomes one validator per field. In form-bench Formik re-renders the whole form on each of 10 keystrokes; here nothing re-renders.

recipes.title: A nested address, posted as nested JSON
recipes.text: Dot-path keys are real fields with their own validators and errors. `nestValues()` builds `{ name, address: { city, zip } }` for the API.

recipes.title: An invite list that grows
recipes.text: `useFieldArray` gives every row a stable key, so removing row two never moves the cursor out of row three.

recipes.title: An edit form that knows when it is saved
recipes.text: After a save, `reset(saved)` makes the server's copy the clean baseline. The Save button is disabled again until the next real change.

faq.q: Is the benchmark measuring the form library or the framework?
faq.a: Both, on purpose. Each library runs in its own framework, written the way its docs recommend, with one shared Zod schema, in real Chromium. That is the cost you ship. It is one overnight run on one machine and we wrote the bench, so the harness is in the repo: `cd examples/form-bench && bun bench-form.ts`.

faq.q: Do I need an adapter for Zod?
faq.a: No. Any Standard Schema (Zod 3.24+, Valibot 1+, ArkType 2+, `@pyreon/validate`) goes straight into `schema`. The `zodSchema()` adapters in `@pyreon/validation` remain for when you want them.

faq.q: What happens to a schema error for a field I didn't declare?
faq.a: It is never dropped. A nested error goes to the closest declared parent field; an error that matches nothing marks the form invalid, sets `submitError` and warns in development.

faq.q: Does it work with server-rendered pages?
faq.a: Yes. The form state is plain signals that start from `initialValues` on both sides, and `focusFirstError()` is a no-op on the server. Input ids come from `createUniqueId()`, which matches between server HTML and the hydrated page from the next release on.

faq.q: Can I watch one value without re-running on every field?
faq.a: `useWatch(form, 'email')` returns that field's own signal. `useFormState(form, (s) => s.isValid && s.isDirty)` takes a selector so a button only recomputes when its inputs change.
